title: Tenant network stub and sequenced upgrade lane for zero-touch airgap onboarding
creator: Asha Menon
description: Background: Several enterprise customers have requested Private/VPC installs that must remain air-gapped but still receive regular runtime and security patches. Current triage workflows expect broad network changes or manual technician work for each upgrade window. This ticket scopes a productized "tenant network stub" artifact and a sequenced, policy-driven upgrade lane to allow semi-automated, zero-touch onboarding and staged upgrades for air-gapped customers with constrained networking. Goal: reduce manual intervention by >70% for patch rollouts to air-gapped customers, surface precise preflight checks, and provide clear fallback lanes to avoid production regressions.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable tenant network stub spec (JSON/YAML) that operators can deploy into customer environments to provide an authenticated pull/telemetry path for staged upgrades is documented and reviewed.
Preflight probe sequence implemented as a checklist that can be executed by customer engineers or automated by operator tooling; each probe has pass/fail guidance and remediation steps.

A 'sequenced upgrade' policy model that supports: canary batch size (percent of tenants), retry/backoff rules, explicit rollback hooks, and dependency checks across DB/storage/networking is defined and validated with 2 internal dry runs.

Console UX: an onboarding flow and upgrade dashboard that shows per-tenant preflight status, expected time windows, and a single-click escalation to manual mode is prototyped in Figma and has PM + Eng + Security signoff.
Runbook and customer communication templates (pre-upgrade notice, outage expectations, rollback comms) exist in Confluence/Drive linked from ticket.
Security sign-off completed documenting allowed minimal network egress destinations, auth patterns, and KMS/HSM constraints.
Pilot with 2 existing air-gapped customers completes with measurable reduction in technician hours and zero customer-facing downtime for non-critical updates.
Metrics: mean time to prepare upgrade decreases by 60%, and number of manual tickets per upgrade decreases by 70% in pilot telemetry.

If pilot shows high adoption, follow-up tickets will cover appliance bridges and managed VPN offerings. Consider funding for a second Solutions Engineering seat for pilot support.
